pages.text: The $(thing)Drying Rack$() is one block tall and holds one 16-leaf inventory. Valid raw leaves can enter from the $(thing)top or horizontal sides$(); bottom insertion is blocked. A hopper underneath can extract only when the batch has completely finished curing.

Rack automation still obeys batch rules: leaves must match the stored leaf's exact item/components, the rack holds at most 16, and insertion is blocked once progress reaches 10%. Bottom-facing vanilla hoppers pull only finished output; compatible Forge logistics use the rack's validated handlers without bypassing those rules.
pages.title: Drying Rack
Production Monitor
pages.text: Place the $(item)Production Monitor$() with its front face pointing at the adjacent transport it should read; it counts confirmed throughput without moving items. It supports vanilla Hoppers. The ghost Filter can be set in the menu or directly on the operator-facing filter target: hover the target for a highlight, use an item to copy it without consuming the stack, or use an empty hand there to clear it. Items mode counts item quantity; Stacks measures 64-item stack-equivalents; Transfers counts successful transfer operations.

pages.title: Monitor Targets & Output
pages.text: Set a numeric target, then choose Keep Counting, Stop Counting, or Reset Count. Reset Count preserves overflow. Output may be None, a Pulse per target crossing, or Hold until reset; Reset Count + Hold becomes Pulse. Manual Reset keeps the rolling rate, and optional External Reset reacts only to a rising redstone edge. A Comparator reports progress.

The $(thing)Hookah$() exposes its three-slot item handler to Forge automation. Tall two-block Hookahs resolve both halves to the same lower master inventory, so Hoppers and compatible Forge item handlers can connect at either level. Inputs remain validated per slot: fuel, Shisha Tobacco, and Water/Dirty Hookah Water.
pages.title: Hookah

pages.text: The $(thing)Tobacco Barrel$() holds up to 64 compatible cured leaves or loose tobacco and exposes validated automation. Extraction preserves tobacco metadata; actively fermenting batches remain protected from premature automated extraction. Display Links can also report the current batch count out of 64.
pages.title: Barrel
Other Processing Blocks
pages.text: The Drying Racks, Tobacco Barrel, Flue Firebox, and Hookah expose validated Forge item automation where appropriate. Automation never bypasses the blocks' normal input, batch, curing, fuel, or slot rules.

pages.title: Hanging Tobacco
pages.text: Traditional hanging 16-leaf bunches are not inventory machines. Hoppers and item handlers cannot insert or extract from them. Break the bunch to recover its leaves.

pages.title: Tobacco Crates
pages.text: Tobacco Crates are packaged blocks rather than live inventories.
